requirement:
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST warn about every
item without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, except items inside a module named `tests`. A warning MUST NOT fail
validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read Git history.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.references.coverage.report`. I found no gap.

- **`habeas status` warns about every item without recent coverage, naming file, line, kind and name.**
  - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[status_shows_coverage_warnings_and_says_when_history_is_incomplete]` asserts a `## Coverage warnings` section. It asserts the exact warning text for `render` in `src/lib.rs`: file, line, `function render has no recent coverage`. It also asserts that the covered `parse` is not warned about.
  - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item]` checks the full warned set at each stage with `warned()`. That set is `["helper"]`, then `["parse","helper"]` after the third re-authoring. This covers the `coverage.reauthored` example, where the third version keeps `parse` covered, and the `coverage.new_function` example, where `helper` is warned about at once.
- **`habeas author` warns after it finishes.**
  - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[habeas_author_prints_coverage_warnings_on_stderr]` runs the binary. It asserts the `helper` warning with file, line, kind and name on stderr, and nothing about coverage on stdout.
  - `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` checks the warning for an orphan function when nothing is assessed.
  - `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_authors_citation_reviews_and_preserves_current_ones]` and `dumb_terminal_keeps_plain_batch_diagnostics` check the report after a batch and after a single-subject `--stdout` run.
- **Items inside a module named `tests` are excluded.**
  - The `project()` fixture has an inline `mod tests { fn fixture() {} }`, and `warned()` never lists `fixture`.
  - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[items_in_out_of_line_tests_modules_are_not_warned_about]` covers `src/foo/tests.rs` and `src/bar/tests/mod.rs`.
  - `src/coverage_history.rs#fn[files_declared_as_tests_modules_are_in_a_tests_module]` checks the path classification with positive and negative cases.
  - `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[a_test_without_a_test_reference_is_an_error_not_a_coverage_warning]` checks that a bare `#[test]` is an error, and that a helper in the same file is a warning rather than an error.
- **A warning does not fail validation.** The reauthoring test asserts that `validate_repository` has no error mentioning `parse` while `parse` is warned about. The batch tests assert `report.errors.is_empty()` while warnings exist.
- **Repository validation does not read Git history.** `tests/coverage.rs#fn[validation_does_not_read_git_history]` deletes the Git object directories. It asserts that validation errors are unchanged, and that `coverage_warnings` then reports `incomplete`.
- **Incomplete history is stated.** This belongs to `requirements.references.coverage.history`. The shallow-clone status test, the `dumb_terminal_keeps_plain_batch_diagnostics` test and the single-subject `--stdout` run in `batch_authors_citation_reviews_and_preserves_current_ones` assert the message.

The only residual doubt is that the tests exercise the "kind" in the warning only for functions. The requirement's wording ties which items need coverage to `requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, which is not assessed here. I did not treat this as a gap.

{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
the commands of {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report` MUST say that
coverage history is incomplete.
:::{example} coverage.reauthored
Function `parse` has no reference, and the evidence of `requirements.cli.check`
read it. The requirement is re-authored and committed twice, and neither new
record reads `parse`. With the default window of 3, the record's third most
recent version still names `parse`, so `habeas status` does not warn. After a
third such commit, no version in the window names it, and `habeas status` warns
about `parse`. {test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.new_function
A new function `helper` has no reference, and no evidence record has ever read
it. `habeas status` warns about it at once; nothing in any window names it.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.test_module
A helper function inside `mod tests` has no reference and is read by no record.
`habeas status` does not warn about it. A `#[test]` function in the same module
without a `{test}` reference is still a validation error.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.tests`
